original.target_description: Study 1, undergraduate visual global/local/control priming; breadth of categorization, 3(Typicality) × 3(Processing Style) interaction reported at supplied p. 112 locator.

n.quote: For each of the 10 main studies, 60
n.sample_role: Participants in Study 1; three between-participant priming conditions in the reported ANOVA.
n.exclusions: No Study 1 exclusions reported; analytic inclusion supported by reported F(4,114) and F(2,57), rather than a separate post-exclusion n statement.

replication.target_description: Experiment 2, MTurk US participants; one-sided independent-samples Bayesian t-test of global versus local priming on mean typicality ratings for 12 fringe exemplars (BOC creativity score).

n.sample_role: Analytic MTurk participants, global versus local conditions; 454 per condition.
n.exclusions: 1307 recruited; 221 discarded following IP-address consistency check, leaving 1086 viable; 90 excluded for Navon error rate >25%, 10 for typicality ratings >2.5 SD from condition mean, and 10 local data sets for condition balance; first 908 of remaining 976 used under stopping rule (manuscript pp. 21–22).

es.quote: The Bayesian t-test yielded BF01 = 10.35 after including 908 participants (N = 454 per condition)

reported_success.location: cached manuscript pp. 22–23, Confirmatory Analysis conclusion
reported_success.quote: We conclude that the results of Experiment 2 support the null hypothesis that, in the present context, global priming does not elicit inflated mean typicality ratings relative to local priming.

notes: Original p. 112 locator identifies the typicality × processing-style interaction. The distinct fringe-exemplar processing-style main effect is printed in Figure 2A, p. 113: F (2, 57) = 8.93; p < .05; it is not paired with the interaction p-value here. Original n=60 is explicitly reported for each main study and consistent with both tests, but no separate post-exclusion analytic-n statement is printed. Original paper title and DOI verified in retrieved full PDF. Replication cached title and author list match supplied reference; cache uses manuscript pagination (results pp. 16–17 and 22–23), rather than supplied published pp. e85/e87 or PDF pp. 6/8. Replication p-values are the authors’ frequentist one-tailed comparisons of the same conditions, outcome and analytic sample as the Bayesian tests; no p-value is assigned to the Bayes factor itself. Cached manuscript abstract says BF01 = 10.84, whereas Experiment 2 confirmatory results and General Discussion say 10.35; extracted 10.35 from the target results section without resolving or converting this internal discrepancy.
